Subject: Private deployment: network isolation checklist + proposed test matrix

Hi Stefan / Elena,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion and helpful clarity on your security constraints. Per our notes, I wanted to summarize next steps, call out the differences we see vs hyperscaler-managed options, and propose a light test matrix so your infra team can validate feasibility without a full POC right away.

Quick recap (from our side):
- Primary constraint: inference hosts must not have outbound access to the public internet; all control-plane communication needs to traverse explicit private connectivity (PrivateLink/VPC peering/VPN).
- Secondary constraints: audit logs retained for 12 months; KMS integration for key material; MFA for console access.

How Redwood compares (short):
- Hyperscalers (e.g., SageMaker, Vertex AI): often easier to spin up, but typically require either public control-plane endpoints or complex private endpoint setups (PrivateLink, VPC SC) that can add configuration and cost.
- Redwood Private: we offer two control-plane modes for private deployments — (1) customer-hosted control plane (deployed into your account/VPC), or (2) isolated control-plane proxy over PrivateLink/VPN with no egress from inference hosts. Both are designed to meet air-gap-like constraints; the customer-hosted option gives you the strongest isolation and auditability.

Proposed minimal test matrix (can run in 2–5 business days):
1) Connectivity: verify inference VM has no outbound internet (block 0.0.0.0/0) and confirm control-plane reachability via PrivateLink endpoint or VPN. Expected outcome: control-plane calls succeed only over private path.
2) Keying: demonstrate KMS-encrypted model artifacts and test key rotation. Expected outcome: model load succeeds, rotated key fails until re-granted.
3) Logging: confirm that audit events (model loads, inference calls) are delivered to your SIEM via a private forwarder. Expected outcome: full event stream for 30k requests/day sample.
4) Failover: simulate control-plane unavailability and validate automatic local fallback to cached model/weights for 5 minutes. Expected outcome: inference continues with degraded metrics but no data exfiltration.

I've attached a short checklist and a brief competitor comparison to help your architects. If the tests above look right, can you confirm who on your infra team should be our point person to coordinate a 2–3 hour window? Our proposed slots: Wed 8/18 afternoon (PST) or Thu 8/19 morning.

Attachments: redwood-network-isolation-checklist.xlsx; redwood-vs-hyperscaler-comparison-brief.pdf

Thanks — I can prep temporary credentials and a lightweight control-plane image for the customer-hosted mode so you can triage without changing production networking.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Aditya —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our security team before we schedule tests:
1) When you say "customer-hosted control plane" — does that require any outbound DNS resolution to redwood-managed domains, or can the control plane be fully inside our VPC with static IPs?
2) For PrivateLink mode, do your agents initiate connections outbound from our VPC, or does Redwood accept inbound PrivateLink endpoints (we prefer the latter so we don't have to open outbound flows).
3) On the failover test: we cannot accept any callbacks to public endpoints during degraded mode. Is your local cache capable of serving inference without contacting Redwood for telemetry or accounting (we can get telemetry through a pull model later)?

Also, we're actively evaluating an alternative path on AWS that uses SageMaker with PrivateLink + Transit Gateway. The selling point from our infra team is single-vendor operational familiarity; their concerns are about edge-case isolation and longer-term cost. Your brief comparing approaches was helpful, but our architects want a hands-on test that matches our exact firewall posture.

If you can answer (1)-(3) above and confirm we can run the connectivity test with zero outbound internet egress from inference hosts, we'll pick the Wed/Thu slot.

Hi team — looping in a short technical plan that addresses Stefan's questions. I'll be available during the proposed slots to run the tests with your infra engineer.

Answers to Stefan's questions:
1) Customer-hosted control plane: can be fully inside your VPC. No mandatory outbound DNS to redwood-managed domains is required — all components talk to local private IPs or PrivateLink endpoints. For convenience we provide an allowlist if you prefer DNS-based resolution, but it's optional.

2) PrivateLink mode: Redwood can accept inbound PrivateLink endpoints (we create an NLB in our control plane which your account peers via PrivateLink). There is no requirement for our agents to initiate arbitrary outbound connections from your inference hosts.

3) Local cache / offline inference: our runtime supports an on-host KV cache and model shard caching. For the short failover window (5–15 minutes) inference will continue entirely locally; telemetry can be buffered locally and pushed via an approved egress path later (or pulled via a scheduled job). No callbacks to public endpoints are required for serving during that window.

Firewall / routing checklist (high-level):
- Inference hosts: deny 0.0.0.0/0 outbound. Allow egress only to your PrivateLink endpoints or to the NLB internal IPs (TCP 443 for control-plane RPC).
- KMS: allow calls to your KMS endpoint (regional) via private endpoint or VPC endpoint.
- SIEM forwarder: allow outbound to your log-collector via private connection (we can deliver via S3 (VPC endpoint) if preferred).
- DNS: use AmazonRoute53 Resolver endpoints or your internal DNS (no public resolution required).

Proposed test steps (detailed):
A) Pre-check: verify routing table and NACLs block public egress; collect traceroutes.
B) Control-plane validation: deploy a lightweight control-plane container into your test VPC (we can push image to your ECR or provide OCI tarball). Confirm TLS handshake on private IP only.
C) Load KMS-encrypted model from S3 via VPC endpoint and validate model signature.
D) Simulated outage: block PrivateLink traffic at the ALB/NLB for 5 minutes and confirm inference continues locally.

I've attached an XLSX checklist that enumerates exact firewall ports, packet flow diagrams, and the minimal IAM policy. I'll bring a prepared checklist during the run so infra can tick the boxes.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
